units: <cite ref="Mishnah Bava Metzia 4:4">B. Mets. IV, 4</cite> <he>אין אונאה לת׳</he> the law of overreaching (<cite ref="A00722"><he>אוֹנָאָה</he></cite>) does not apply to a merchant, opp. <cite ref="E00117"><he>הדיוט</he></cite> a private person; expl.

ib. 51ᵃ בת׳ ספסר, v. סַפְסָר; ib. מאי אין לת׳ אונאה אינו וכ׳ ‘onaah does not apply to a merchant’ means, that the regulations concerning onaah do not apply to him, and he may withdraw from the purchase even if the difference is less than the law prescribes.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 52a">Ib. 52ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Tosefta Bava Metzia 3:19">Tosef. ib. III, 19</cite>, v. <cite ref="H01717"><he>חָרָם</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Metzia 4:12">B. Mets. IV, 12</cite>; a. fr.—Pl. <he>תַּגָּרִים</he>, <he>תַּגָּרִין</he>.
B. Bath. 75ᵃ (ref. to Job XL, 30) ואין כנענים אלא ת׳ by k’naʿănim merchants are meant.
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Metzia 4:3">B. Mets. IV, 3</cite> <he>תַּגָּרֵי לוד</he> the vendors of Lydda.
<cite ref="Pesachim 50b:7">Pes. 50ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>ת׳ סימטא</he>, v. <cite ref="O00700"><he>סִימְטָא</he> I</cite>.

<cite ref="Pesachim 50b:10">Ib.</cite> <he>הן ותַגָּרֵיהֶן ותגרי תגריהן</he> they (the writers of sacred books &c.), and the traders to whom they sell, and the traders to whom the traders sell; <cite ref="Tosefta Bikkurim 2:15">Tosef. Bicc. II, 15</cite>.
<cite ref="Eruvin 55a">Erub. 55ᵃ</cite> (ed. Sonc. <he>תַּגְּרָנִין</he>); <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 940">Yalk. Deut. 940</cite>; a. fr.
